title: Clinical Mastery: Exposure Keratopathy
summary: Exposure keratopathy is a sight-threatening condition resulting from incomplete eyelid closure (lagophthalmos), leading to ocular surface desiccation, epithelial breakdown, and potential stromal ulceration. Prompt identification and aggressive lubrication are mandatory to prevent visual morbidity.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Exposure keratopathy results from a failure of the eyelid to provide adequate coverage of the globe. This disrupts the tear film, causing increased evaporation and hyperosmolarity. Without the blink-induced distribution of mucins and lipids, the corneal epithelium undergoes desiccation, shedding, and keratinization. In severe cases, secondary microbial keratitis occurs due to breach of the ocular surface barrier.

rows: Lax upper lids, chronic papillary conjunctivitis

sections.title: Red Flags: Emergency Status
content: Infiltrate or stromal thinning (risk of perforation)
Decreased visual acuity (involvement of visual axis)
Ocular pain disproportionate to findings (risk of globe integrity loss)

sections.title: Clinical Examination Sequence
content: Step 1: Assess Bell's phenomenon (upward globe rotation on closure).
Step 2: Measure lagophthalmos gap in mm using a millimeter ruler.
Step 3: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy with Fluorescein staining to evaluate interpalpebral epithelial defects.
Step 4: Check corneal sensation with a cotton-wisp test (r/o neurotrophic component).
Step 5: Exophthalmometry (Hertel) to rule out underlying proptosis.

sections.title: Management Protocol
content: Mechanical: Taping eyelids closed during sleep.
Surgical: Temporary tarsorrhaphy, gold weight implants, or lower lid tightening.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always check the 'Bell's Phenomenon'. Patients lacking this are at extreme risk for corneal perforation.
Preservative-free preparations are mandatory if frequency exceeds 4x/day to prevent toxic epitheliopathy.
In ICU patients, consider the 'Vaseline technique' or clear plastic occlusive dressings to maintain moisture.
Gold weight implant (e.g., 0.8g to 1.6g) is the gold standard for facial nerve palsy-induced lagophthalmos.
Surgical correction should not be delayed if medical management fails to show epithelial healing within 48-72 hours.
